A silver Roman finger ring, Henig Type VIII, of which only the bezel and shoulders survive. The ring bezel is circular and the shoulders are also circular. The hoop is missing. The shoulders are decorated with an incised 'V' with perimeter facets to either side decorated with radiating incised lines. The bezel bears the inscription 'TO', which is an abbreviation for the Celtic god-name Totatis, one of the principal deities in Gaul. Many of these rings are known from the East Midlands, especially in Lincolnshire where the deity appears to have had a large following.
